iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has a modular causal structure with 6 inputs and 4 outputs. Y3 depends only on X1 and X3 (approximately linear: Y3 ≈ 0.077 + 0.49*X1 + 0.44*X3, R²=0.90, with mild synergistic interaction at extremes). Y4 depends on X2 (strongest positive), X4 (positive, synergistic with X2 via 10x amplification), X6 (negative), and X1 (very weak positive). Y1 is a complex nonlinear function of all 6 inputs: X2 is the strongest driver via a powerful X2*X4 synergistic interaction (13x amplification), X5 has a sigmoid threshold at ~0.4 fully saturated above 0.6 (confirmed gradient <0.001 at X5≥0.8), X6 is positive at high X5 but flips negative at low X5 (X5*X6 interaction), and X1/X3 provide weak positive contributions. Y2 depends on X3 (strongest reducer), X2 (strongest increaser), X1 (weak reducer), X4 and X6 (both exhibit sign-reversing interactions with X2, crossovers at X2≈0.7). X5 has no meaningful effect on Y2. The Pareto front is a smooth 2D surface parameterized by (X2, X6) with X1=X3=X4=1 and X5≥0.6 fixed at globally optimal values. X2 drives the primary Y1/Y4 vs Y2 trade-off. At high X2 (≥0.7), increasing X6 simultaneously increases Y1 AND decreases Y2 (free lunch) while only moderately reducing Y4, creating a favorable trade-off region. All 79 Pareto-optimal points satisfy Y3≥0.997 (well above the 0.4 threshold).
